messages.author: 7fc4e6d7d3655d9d
messages.subject: MIMIC model proper syntax?
parts:
Hello I am looking to specify a MIMIC model in Lavaan. I have two questions:
1. Are the formative measures to be written utilizing a regression syntax for a mimic model in lavaan? Here is an example of how I specified a mimic model in Lavaan to date:
Model1 <- 'V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
                   V1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3'

Side information: I understand that the formative syntax for Lavaan uses the <~ operator such that if I were to use this for a MIMC model then my previously proposed model would look like this:
Model 1<- 'V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
                    V1 <~ X1 + X2 + X3'

For me, I get drastically different fit statistics between the two models. The first model using the regression syntax has great fit statistics, the second model using the formative syntax has very poor fit statistics. I would like to understand which syntax is proper before I go trying to interpret the output.

2. Where can I find information or examples of MIMIC modesl utilizing Lavaan? I really cannot seem to find much information on MIMIC models with Lavaan. 


Thanks! 
Jessica

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC model proper syntax?
parts:
Re (1) This is hardly surprising. Look at the df of the two models.  Model1 has 6 df and Model2 7 df. If you now examine the parameter tables, you will see that V1 ~~ V1 is not freely estimated for Model2. If you add V1 ~~ V1 to this model, you will get the same results as with Model1.

Here is a sample code to show this:


library(lavaan)

# Some strange data
set.seed(1234)
Va <- rnorm(1000)
Vb <- 0.9 * Va + rnorm(1000)
Vc <- 0.9 * Va + rnorm(1000)
X1 <- 0.2 * Va + rnorm(1000)
X2 <- 0.3 * Va + rnorm(1000)
X3 <- 0.4 * Va + rnorm(1000)
myData <- data.frame(Va = Va, Vb = Vb, Vc = Vc, X1 = X1, X2 = X2, X3 = X3)

myModel1 ='

V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
V1 ~ X1 + X2 + X3'
myModel2 ='

V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
V1 <~ X1 + X2 + X3'

fit1 <- sem(myModel1, myData)
fit2 <- sem(myModel2, myData)

fitMeasures(fit1, c("chisq", "df"))
fitMeasures(fit2, c("chisq", "df"))

parameterTable(fit1)
parameterTable(fit2)

myModel3 ='

V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
V1 <~ X1 + X2 + X3

V1 ~~ V1'

fit3 <- sem(myModel3, myData)

fitMeasures(fit3, c("chisq", "df"))


I see no reason to fix V1 =~ Va and V1 ~~ V1 (Model2 without modification).

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: MIMIC model proper syntax?
parts:
The syntax is irrelevant for lavaan (myModel2 and myModel3 are identical). The syntax that is easier to read for humans should be preferred. If you are looking for some kind of standard, keep in mind that the label "V1" does not really signal that V1 is a factor. Detached from this, you could also think about this version:

myModel4 ='

V1 =~ Va + Vb + Vc
V1 <~ X1 + X2 + X3'

fit4 <- sem(myModel4, myData, std.lv = TRUE)

Now identification is achieved via std.lv (V1 ~~  V1 fixed) and V1 =~ Va is freely estimated.
